sentences.text:
And Others
 Versus
 Kamal And Anr. And Others
 Appearance:
Ms. Minu Rajpal - Advocate for the appellants.
Shri Akshansh Mehra - Advocate for respondent No.2.

Order 
1. The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 1/7/2011 passed in Claim Case No.209/2010 whereby the deduction of the income of the deceased and exclusion of certain parts of the earning of the deceased have been put into question.
2. The liability of the Insurance Company is not under dispute.
Also the death of the deceased in the accident is not under challenge.
3. Short facts giving rise to the case are that on 1/4/2010 at around 10.30 AM the deceased Hari Singh was going from his motorcycle from Gandwani at his home.

When he reached Chorpwadi Manawar Kukshi road, respondent No.1 came driving his motorcycle bearing registration No.M.P. 11 MD 5065 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the deceased from behind because of which he sustained grievous injuries.

He was rushed NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17289 2 MA-2204-2011 to Community Health Centre, Kukshi from where he was referred to District Hospital, Barwani but on the way to the said hospital he died.
4. The appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 claiming compensation for the death of the deceased Hari Singh in the above mentioned accident.
The claims tribunal after considering the evidence on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.14,15,040/- to the appellants.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants by referring to para 12 of the impugned award submits that while assessing the income of the deceased only his basic pay has been taken into consideration.
She Smt. Relambai And 2 Ors. vs Kamal And Anr.

1 submits that deceased was working as Senior Lineman in the erstwhile M.P. Electricity Board.
At the time of his death he was receiving pay of Rs.20,999/- per month.

The claims tribunal while considering the income of the deceased has taken only the basic salary of the deceased into account at Rs.13,510/- while doing so 20% deduction on account of income tax has also been made.
Thus the total income of the deceased was taken at Rs.1,61,120/- and by taking this amount the loss of dependency was calculated at Rs.14,05,040/-.
Apart from this an amount of Rs.10000/- was awarded in all other heads.
Thus a total sum of Rs.14,05,040/- was awarded to the appellants.

She submits that exclusion of the dearness and other allowance from the salary of the deceased for taking the factor of income by only adopting the basic salary of the deceased is not correct and proper.

For buttressing her submission she relied on the recent decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Meenakshi V/s. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd , 2020 INSC 573 (Neutral NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17289 3 MA-2204-2011 Citation).

entities.text: Meenakshi V/s. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd , 2020 INSC 573 (Neutral NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17289 3 MA-2204-2011 Citation)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By referring to para 7, 9, 10 and 12 of the same she submits that the Hon'ble Apex Court has clearly held that dearness allowance and house rent allowance payable to the deceased should have been included for determining the income of the deceased.

She further submits that a deduction of 20% for income tax is also not correct and proper in view of the fact that the income slab of the deceased in view of his salary would fall in the initial slab of 10%.
She further submits that for loss of consortium nothing has been awarded as a total compensation of Rs.10000/- has been awarded in all other heads to all the three claimants / appellants.
She also submits that nothing for funeral expenses and loss of estate has been awarded.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 / Insurance Company submits that the claims tribunal has correctly deducted 20% from the income of the deceased for income tax deductions and also submits that the basic salary of the deceased has been taken into account.
All the other allowances are only incidental thus they have correctly been excluded from the consideration while assessing the income of the deceased.
Thus he supports the findings of the tribunal.
7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

From discussion made by the claims tribunal in para 12 of the award, it is seen that while accepting the salary of the appellant at Rs.20,999/-, in view of the service record Exhibits P/10 to P/12 and pay slip Exhibit P/13, the claims tribunal has concluded that the basic salary of the deceased is Rs.13,510/-.
Thus only this part of the pay has been taken as income of the deceased excluding everything else.
The claims tribunal while assessing the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17289 4 MA-2204-2011 income has not even included the component of dearness allowance and house rent allowance.

Whereas the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Meenakshi (supra) has clearly held in para 7 of the order as under :-
"7.

We therefore, are of the opinion that "dearness allowance" and "house rent allowance" payable to the deceased should have been included for determining the income of the deceased and consequently the amount of compensation."
8.
Thus in the considered view of this Court in the income of the deceased, the component of dearness allowance and house rent allowance are required to be added.
After adding these amounts the income of the deceased comes to Rs.16961/-.
In terms of salary of the deceased the slab which would be applicable for payment of income tax would fall within the category of 10%.
Thus Smt. Relambai And 2 Ors. vs Kamal And Anr.

2 deduction in that behalf is done at 10%.
Thus the net income of the deceased would come to Rs.15,270/-.
Looking to the age of the deceased at 47/48 years, 25% is to be added for future prospects.
Thus the total compensation commensurated to the income above assessed would come to Rs.19,85,100/- for loss of dependency.
As it can be seen from the findings of the award nothing has been paid for loss of consortium.
Although the appellants are wife, daughter and son of the deceased.
Thus all of them are entitled for payment of consortium in terms of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram 2018 (18) SCC 130 .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus all three of them are awarded Rs.40000/- each which would total Rs.1,20,000/-.
For loss of estate and funeral expenses Rs.15000/- each is awarded.
Thus the total compensation would come to Rs.21,35,100/-.
The claims tribunal has already awarded a compensation of Rs.14,15,040/-.

Thus after deducting the same the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17289 5 MA-2204-2011 appellants are entitled for payment of Rs.7,27,060/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.

The enhanced amount shall carry the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of application of the award but excluding the period from 22/5/2024 to 14/9/2024 for which the appeal remained dismissed for want of prosecution.
9. The appellant have valued the appeal at Rs.6.50 lacs.
Thus the appellants have to pay deficit court fees within a period of one month from today.
10. With the above terms, the appeal stands allowed and disposed off.
No orders as to cost.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
